assessment.rationale: No open or discoverable solution repairs mitochondria in every cell, so the Main KPI of 1,000,000,000 people with repaired mitochondria is far from met. The one approved mitochondria-targeted drug, elamipretide (Forzinity), received US accelerated approval in September 2025 for Barth syndrome only, on a knee-extensor strength endpoint and conditional on a confirmatory trial; its primary mitochondrial myopathy and dry-AMD programmes did not win approval (https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2025/10/fda-approval-for-mitochondrial-therapeutic-elamipretide-formerly-ss-31/). Mitochondrial transplantation in humans is a single unreviewed 2026 case report of autologous muscle mitochondria injected into one patient's eyes, safe but with no measurable acuity gain (https://sciencealert.com/world-first-mitochondria-from-a-womans-leg-were-injected-into-her-eyes), alongside a 6-participant safety study (NCT04548843) and mouse/monkey encapsulated-mitochondria work. The nearest consumer-scale option, urolithin A, gives modest and inconsistent muscle endurance and strength gains in small industry-funded trials of 66 and 88 participants (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9133463/), which is not cell-wide mitochondrial repair. Open source exists only upstream of therapy: mtDNA base-editing design and analysis code such as https://github.com/YangLab/eTALED_computational_analysis and the MitoEdit pipeline. Honest limit: a simple systemic therapy remains unsolved, but tasks that only re-run urolithin A or elamipretide-style regimens, or re-implement published mtDNA editing design tools, are known answers and need their own basis.

additionalSearches.query: elamipretide FDA approval status 2026 mitochondrial disease
additionalSearches.finding: Elamipretide (Forzinity) won FDA accelerated approval in September 2025 for Barth syndrome only, an ultra-rare disorder, on a muscle-strength surrogate and conditional on a confirmatory trial begun in 2026. No approved therapy repairs mitochondria generally; primary mitochondrial myopathy and dry-AMD trials did not lead to approval.

additionalSearches.query: mitochondrial transplantation therapy human trial 2026 results
additionalSearches.finding: Human mitochondrial transplantation in 2026 is one non-peer-reviewed case report: autologous leg-muscle mitochondria injected into both eyes of a single patient, safe with a transient pupillary response and no acuity change. Other work is a 6-participant safety study (NCT04548843) and preclinical mouse/monkey encapsulated-mitochondria and MitoCatch targeting studies.

additionalSearches.query: urolithin A mitophagy clinical trial muscle older adults Mitopure evidence
additionalSearches.finding: Urolithin A human trials are small (66 adults aged 65-90; 88 middle-aged adults), short (4 months), Amazentis-funded, and show modest muscle endurance and about 12 percent strength gains with several null endpoints including hand-grip. No large independent confirmatory trial and no demonstration of repaired mitochondria across cells.

additionalSearches.query: open source mitochondrial DNA base editing mitochondria gene therapy github
additionalSearches.finding: Open-source mitochondrial work is design and analysis software only: eTALED editing-efficiency and off-target analysis scripts, and the MitoEdit pipeline for choosing mtDNA target bases. No open-source mitochondrial therapy, delivery system or clinical programme was found.
